subject: Numeracy
title: Shape hunt
objectives: Children will find and name a circle, a square and a triangle in the environment.
Children will build a simple picture using shapes with support.
content: Revising circle, square and triangle, finding shapes indoors and outdoors and building simple pictures with shapes.
teachingActivities: Ask children to describe the shape using touch and simple talk; use the shape names every time; leave shape cards on show for the week.
learnerActivities: Hunt for shapes, match shape cards to real objects, build pictures and say which shape they see.
assessment: Check whether each child names or points to circle, square and triangle with growing accuracy.
expectedOutcomes: Names or points to the three shapes with growing accuracy.
crossCurricular: Understanding the world: shapes in buildings

lessons.title: Shape hunt indoors
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find circles, squares and triangles in the room.
successCriteria: Finds a shape that matches the card
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can find circles, squares and triangles with support and sort them into three groups.
resources: Large shape cards: circle, square, triangle
Objects of different shapes around the room
lessons.starter: Hold up the circle card and ask "Where is a circle in our room?" Wait for a child to point and say "Yes! A clock, a circle."
teacherActivities: Show each shape card and name it. Trace the edge slowly with a finger.
Give each pair a shape card and say "Go and find the same shape."
When children find a match, ask "What shape is it?"
Gather in a circle and let each pair show what they found.
learnerActivities: Children trace the shape in the air.
Pairs walk around and find a matching object.
Child names or shows the shape.
Pairs show their object and say the shape.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each shape card and name it. Trace the edge slowly with a finger. Children: Children trace the shape in the air.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each pair a shape card and say "Go and find the same shape." Children: Pairs walk around and find a matching object.
Step 3. Teacher: When children find a match, ask "What shape is it?" Children: Child names or shows the shape.
Step 4. Teacher: Gather in a circle and let each pair show what they found. Children: Pairs show their object and say the shape.

practical.title: Room shape hunt
steps: Give each pair a shape card.
Find an object in the room with the same shape.
Bring it to the mat or point to it.
practical.safety: Keep the walkways clear; children walk and carry only one object each; no climbing to reach objects.

differentiation.support: Hunt for only one shape, such as the circle, with an adult.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find two different objects with the same shape.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put all found objects in a row and say the shape of each one.
lessons.homeConnection: Find circles, squares and triangles at home on plates, windows and tiles.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find circles, squares and triangles in the room" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: A clock, a window and a roof
learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Shape, shape, where is the shape? Round, square, triangle, find the shape.

lessons.title: Shape hunt outdoors
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find shapes in the school compound or playground.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can find circles, squares and triangles with support and sort them into three groups.
resources: A clipboard or card with three shapes
lessons.starter: Take the shape cards outside and say "Let us look for shapes outside. A wheel, a window, a roof. Which shape?"
teacherActivities: Stand together and hold up each shape card. Ask "What can we find like this?"
Walk to a wheel or a round gate and say "A circle!" Trace it in the air.
Find a square window and a triangle roof with the children.
Give each child a shape card and let them find a match.
learnerActivities: Children look around and point to objects.
Children trace the shape and say "circle".
Children point and name each shape.
Child finds a matching shape outside and shows a friend.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Stand together and hold up each shape card. Ask "What can we find like this?" Children: Children look around and point to objects.
Step 2. Teacher: Walk to a wheel or a round gate and say "A circle!" Trace it in the air. Children: Children trace the shape and say "circle".
Step 3. Teacher: Find a square window and a triangle roof with the children. Children: Children point and name each shape.
Step 4. Teacher: Give each child a shape card and let them find a match. Children: Child finds a matching shape outside and shows a friend.

practical.title: Outdoor shape walk
steps: Walk with a partner around a safe area.
Look for shapes that match the card.
Tell the group what you found.
practical.safety: Keep the walk within a fenced area with an adult for every four children; stay away from roads and water; wash hands afterwards.

differentiation.support: Walk beside the child and point to suitable shapes.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count how many circles they can find.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Return indoors and wash hands. Say "Shape hunters, well done."
lessons.homeConnection: On the way home, point out shapes of doors, signs and wheels.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find shapes in the school compound or playground" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?

lessons.title: Build with shapes
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will build a simple house or vehicle using shapes.
successCriteria: Uses at least two shapes to build
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can find circles, squares and triangles with support and sort them into three groups.
resources: Large wooden blocks of different shapes
lessons.starter: Build a quick house with a square block and a triangle block on top. Say "A square for the walls and a triangle for the roof. What shapes can you use?"
teacherActivities: Show a house made of shapes and name each shape you used.
Give each child a few blocks and ask them to build their own house.
Ask "What shapes did you use?" and walk around.
Invite children to visit a friend’s house and say one shape they see.
learnerActivities: Children point to each shape and name it.
Child builds a simple house.
Child names or points to the shapes used.
Children look at each other’s buildings and name a shape.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a house made of shapes and name each shape you used. Children: Children point to each shape and name it.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child a few blocks and ask them to build their own house. Children: Child builds a simple house.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "What shapes did you use?" and walk around. Children: Child names or points to the shapes used.
Step 4. Teacher: Invite children to visit a friend’s house and say one shape they see. Children: Children look at each other’s buildings and name a shape.

practical.title: Shape houses
steps: Give each pair a basket of blocks.
Build a house or a car using at least two shapes.
practical.safety: Use large blocks and build on the floor only; keep the area clear and walk around buildings carefully.

differentiation.support: Build together hand-over-hand using only a square and a triangle.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to build a bridge or a tower and name the shapes.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Take a photograph of each building and then tidy the blocks together.
lessons.homeConnection: Build with boxes and cups at home and name the shapes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "build a simple house or vehicle using shapes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Shape pictures with friends
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will make a group picture using shapes and say which shapes they used.
successCriteria: Adds a shape to a group picture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can find circles, squares and triangles with support and sort them into three groups.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we make one big picture together, a village! What shapes can a village have?" Show the large paper.
teacherActivities: Place a square and a triangle on the paper to make a first house. Say the shapes.
Ask each child to add a shape to make a house, a car or a tree.
Glue the shapes down while naming each one.
Look at the finished picture and count how many circles, squares and triangles there are.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say the shapes.
Child places a shape on the paper and names it.
Children help glue with supervision.
Children point and count the shapes.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Place a square and a triangle on the paper to make a first house. Say the shapes. Children: Children watch and say the shapes.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask each child to add a shape to make a house, a car or a tree. Children: Child places a shape on the paper and names it.
Step 3. Teacher: Glue the shapes down while naming each one. Children: Children help glue with supervision.
Step 4. Teacher: Look at the finished picture and count how many circles, squares and triangles there are. Children: Children point and count the shapes.

practical.title: Village picture
steps: Spread a large paper on the floor.
practical.safety: Use non-toxic glue sticks, supervised; wash hands afterwards; keep scissors out of reach.

differentiation.support: Offer one shape at a time and show where to place it.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to add details such as a door or a window and name the shape.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many circles are in our picture?
questions.expected: The number counted, up to five.

expectedOutcomes: Contributes to a group shape picture
lessons.conclusion: Display the picture on the wall and say "Our shape village!"
lessons.homeConnection: Make a picture with paper shapes cut from old cartons.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make a group picture using shapes and say which shapes they used" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?

Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Shape hunt stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show they can find, name and use shapes at three stations.
successCriteria: Names or points to circle, square and triangle
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can find circles, squares and triangles with support and sort them into three groups.
lessons.starter: Sing the shape song and show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Ask "Show me a triangle" and "What shape is this?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station.
Child points to or names a shape.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Show me a triangle" and "What shape is this?" Children: Child points to or names a shape.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Use large shapes and blocks only; supervise glue; keep floors clear.

differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to teach a friend the three shapes.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names or points to circle, square and triangle; finds shapes in the environment; builds with shapes.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 3
Names the three shapes with growing accuracy
lessons.conclusion: Sing the shape song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep naming shapes you see this week.
